curl_note: The script requires Bash, cURL, OpenSSL and base64. Replace ASSET and ACCOUNT in the script, and ensure the signed query is encoded exactly as sent by cURL.
legacy_intro: This directory contains a signed HTTP script for diagnosing the legacy account-secret API. For application integration, use the Python, Go, Java or Node.js SDK.
legacy_config: Create an application in Application Management and authorize the target asset accounts. Set the endpoint, application AK/SK and organization ID below; replace every placeholder with its actual value before running.
targets: The examples query asset ubuntu_docker and account root by default. Replace them in the example with real authorized names. Run commands from the repository root. Example output contains secrets; do not send it to application logs.
legacy_response: The response id identifies the application, not an account revision. A null secret can reflect the server secret-view setting. These examples do not receive credential events, report applied revisions or execute application commands.
legacy_errors: For 401, check AK/SK, organization, host time and the signed URL. For 403, check application status and account authorization. For 400, check asset/account selectors and query encoding. Do not log secrets or Authorization headers. Account names and asset names must match the application’s authorized resources.
policy_access: The signature details and protocol table below are diagnostic references. Use SDK methods for credential policies, or use the Python Agent through JSON files, EnvironmentFile or Unix Socket.
signature: Sign requests with HMAC-SHA256 in the header order below. Include the encoded path and query in request-target, SHA-256 of the exact body in Digest, a unique UUID in X-JMS-Request-ID, an HTTP UTC Date, X-JMS-Client-Version, X-JMS-Protocol-Version: 1 and X-JMS-Config-Schema-Version: 0 for SDKs. API and WebSocket use the application AK/SK and a stable, unique instance_id; refresh the signature for each request or reconnect.
confirmation: For alternating rotation, validate a real connection, switch the application connection pool and release old connections before confirming the exact key, revision and account_id. Credential change subscriptions require no confirmation. A failed connection check must prevent confirmation.
receipts: A received receipt only means an event was read. Send received with event_id on the same WebSocket before handling business events; snapshot and pong require no receipt. Reconcile the snapshot on every connection and reconnect, process credential.updated, and handle revocation or configuration changes.
python_intro: Python 3.9+ provides the credential-policy SDK and Linux Agent. The SDK uses the application AK/SK; the Agent delivers credentials locally so applications in other languages can use them.
agent_setup: Prepare a Linux host with systemd, Python 3.9+ and the application user. Bind the application to a credential policy and authorize its accounts; alternating rotation needs both accounts. In the application Access wizard, select Agent, configure the runtime user, installation path and delivery mode, then download jms_pam_agent.json. Install the downloaded SDK directory and run the command below for the default path; replace placeholders. Each replica needs a stable, unique instance ID.
agent_paths: The default paths are below. Obtain configuration-id from the downloaded bootstrap and credential-key from the policy. The configured installation path can differ. Bootstrap contains AK/SK: restrict access, remove the downloaded bootstrap after installation and keep installed configuration private.
agent_delivery: Choose JSON for files, EnvironmentFile for a pinned systemd service, or Unix Socket for local API access. The Agent records delivered revisions after delivery succeeds; the application validates and applies credentials before recording an applied revision. The socket belongs to the configured application user with mode 0600; make local requests as that user.
agent_environment: The systemd unit must reference the EnvironmentFile. Use reload only if the application rereads it; reload does not inject new environment variables into a running process. Installation pins the allowed paths, user, service and action; expanding them requires reinstallation.
agent_confirm: Only alternating rotation uses confirm. A local confirmation is persisted first; status confirmed means Core accepted it, while pending means it will be retried. Do not confirm merely because a file was written or a service restarted.
recovery: The Agent reconciles on startup, on relevant events and every 300 seconds. Network failures retain the authorized cache. Identity or authorization rejection blocks socket retrieval; successful signed synchronization restores it. Previously written files remain. SIGINT/SIGTERM closes the server, connections and reader thread.
sdk_setup: Create and bind a credential policy, authorize its asset accounts and download jms_pam_config.py from the application Access wizard. Python 3.9+ is required. Install from the repository command below or run python3 -m pip install . in the downloaded SDK directory.
sdk_config: Place jms_pam_config.py next to the application. Its client_options contain application identity material: do not commit or log it. Use one stable, unique instance_id per replica. get_credential accepts exactly one selector: account_id for authorized accounts, or key for a rotation policy.
event_processing: Process both the initial/reconnect snapshot and credential.updated. The example handles subscription and alternating_rotation separately. Implement apply_credential to validate a real connection, switch the application connection pool and release old connections. The placeholder raises an exception so it cannot confirm an unapplied credential.
apply_error: Implement and verify application credential switching
command_processing: Use list_application_commands to poll pending requests and execute_application_command(event, handler) to claim execution. Only an accepted claim runs the handler. A switch handler verifies the requested revision and account, applies the credential and confirms it; a restart handler restarts the application and checks health. Report success only after the work completes. Failed result reporting preserves the original handler exception.
sdk_errors: The client closes HTTP sessions and event streams with with or close. clone creates an independent session. HTTP, network, authentication and decoding failures raise PAMError with code, status_code, detail and original_error. Retry transient errors at the application boundary; handle authorization denial explicitly and keep credentials out of logs.
compatibility: New code uses snake_case keyword methods and dataclass attributes. The original credential.v1 request-object API remains available with DeprecationWarning. SDK version 1 uses the same protocol as the Agent; sync_agent accepts KnownRevision values for cached and delivered revisions.
sdk_receipts: The SDK automatically sends a best-effort received receipt before yielding a business event. No additional receipt is required from the application. A receipt means only that the event was read, not that credentials were applied; it does not replace confirmation. Reconcile the initial and reconnect snapshots; snapshot and pong require no receipt.
native_intro: This SDK follows the Python credential-policy SDK. It retrieves authorized accounts or rotation-policy credentials, confirms applied revisions, watches events, processes application commands and synchronizes Agent state. Request URLs, HMAC signatures, Digest, UTC Date, request IDs and protocol headers are generated by the client.
native_setup: Install the source SDK and use the configuration below. Authorize accounts and bind policies in Application Management; obtain the application AK/SK and organization ID from its access materials. Replace placeholders and keep identity material in deployment secrets. Use a stable, unique instance ID for each replica. Fetch with exactly one selector: account ID or policy key.
native_events: Process initial/reconnect snapshots and credential.updated. The complete event example below handles subscription and alternating_rotation, plus application commands. Replace the credential-application hook: validate a real connection, switch the pool and release old connections. The placeholder throws so an unapplied revision cannot be confirmed. Reconcile removed accounts in snapshots and revocation events in the application cache.
native_commands: Polling, command claiming and outcome reporting are SDK methods. Execute a handler only after an accepted claim. A switch handler validates the requested revision and account, applies the credential, then confirms it. A restart handler restarts the application and checks its health. Report success only after completion; reporting failure preserves the original handler error.
native_errors: HTTP, network, authentication and response decoding failures use the SDK exception/error type with code and HTTP status. Close streams and clients when finished. Clones have independent lifecycles. Retry transient failures at the application boundary and never log secrets or authentication headers.
native_compatibility: All SDKs use protocol version 1; Agent configuration uses schema version 1. A client_upgrade_required response (HTTP 426) requires checking compatibility and upgrading. Unknown optional fields and notification events are tolerated; unsupported policy modes must not be applied or confirmed. Received event receipts are sent automatically and do not prove credential application.
native_agent: Agent synchronization is exposed for Agent implementations. It requires Agent identity/source and a configuration ID, and accepts cached and delivered KnownRevision values. Linux installation, file delivery and local API are currently provided by the Python Agent; applications of any language can use that Agent.
native_install: The SDK packages are currently installed from this repository; they are not published to public package registries. Replace /path/to/jumpserver with an absolute path. Run the Go and Node.js install commands in your application directory, or add the Java dependency to your application pom.xml. Local imports in the runnable repository examples should be replaced by the package imports below.
